header.title: block_output interchange, tiny GPT-2, CPU
header.description: AUTHORED FOR causalab-mini — not copied from causalab, like documents/attention_query_cpu.json and documents/das_cpu_reduction.json. It exists to ask one question: does the engine generalize to a second model family, or only the metrics? It does not ask whether the *result* means anything — the weights are random. minimal_cpu.json cannot be pointed at this checkpoint, because tiny GPT-2's near-character byte-level vocabulary spells ' Friday' as four tokens and a single-token answer metric refuses; so the weekdays table is replaced by documents/data/counting, whose answers (' one' ... ' four') are one token each under that tokenizer. Everything else is minimal_cpu.json's method with one metric: one swap at the last prompt token of layer 2 (the tiny GPT-2 has five layers), one lm_head read, one logit_diff. Unlike the tiny Llama's sentencepiece tokenizer, this one gives ' two' and 'two' different ids, so token_form: space_prefixed is load-bearing here and inert there.
